title: Block: Two Pointers From Both Ends
oneLiner: Check whether a string reads the same both ways, looking only at letters and digits and ignoring case.
keyTakeaway: Two pointers from both ends: skip what doesn't count, compare, step both inward, stop when they meet. Every skip loop needs its own left < right check.
explanation:
Return true if s is a palindrome when you keep only letters and digits and ignore case. "A man, a plan, a canal: Panama" is; "race a car" isn't. An empty string, or one with no letters or digits, is a palindrome.

Put left at 0 and right at the last index. Move each past characters that aren't letters or digits (char.IsLetterOrDigit in C#, str.isalnum in Python), compare the two lowercased characters, then step both inward. Doing it in place avoids building a filtered copy.

gotchas: A skip loop without its own left < right check runs off the end on input like "!!".

complexity.note: Each pointer moves across the string once; only two indices are stored.
